A sprung steel depth gauge presses down from the top, its probe touching the top plate. One directional key light rakes from the left across the assembly, throwing long contact shadows on weathered concrete. Palette: graphite, copper, bone white. Framing: extreme asymmetry, small licence cartridge bottom-left against towering seven-plate stack right. No text, no logos, no lettering.

prompt: Cinematic still, 35mm anamorphic wide. An empty S&OP control room: a large brushed-steel circular planning board mounted on a concrete wall at left, a wall clock with an unmarked dial and two slim hands above it, a long slate-grey meeting table with seven empty chairs. A single overhead industrial lamp from the right rakes warm amber across the table, casting long shadows. Palette: charcoal, bone white, cobalt. Concrete floor, glass partition. Asymmetric low-angle framing with the circular board off-centre left and empty chairs receding right. No people, no text, no lettering, no numerals, no signage. Fine film grain, shallow depth of field, crisp atmospheric depth.

rationale: A cinematic wide shot of a control room/meeting room captures the recurring, systemic nature of the S&OP cycle and its labour cost better than a macro object. Seven chairs stand in for the manager-hours without showing people, and the empty room emphasises the ongoing operational burden.
subject: An empty S&OP control room with a circular planning board, seven chairs, and a wall clock.
core_thesis: The licence is the smallest line in an S&OP programme; the recurring cycle that runs it costs $250,000 to $750,000 a year, so a module earns its keep only by removing hours from that cycle.
core_conflict: Recurring planning-cycle labour hours versus software licence price, where review features add hours instead of removing them.
composition: Asymmetric low-angle with the circular board off-centre left and empty chairs receding right
